Analysis of credit card transactions finds that sporting goods purchases ramp up earlier than other categories, driven in part by hunting season

MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Based on an analysis of credit card transactions processed across a sample of about 50,000 small- and medium-sized retail merchants from 2022 through 2025, Deluxe Corporation (NYSE: DLX) found that while sporting-goods retailers who carry hunting equipment bagged their biggest haul around Thanksgiving, beauty, apparel, and accessory purchases increased sharply in the final two weeks before Christmas.

The boost in sporting goods transactions is likely due to the start of hunting season overlapping with Black Friday in many states, as well as to end-of-year rebates offered by hunting and outdoor adventure equipment manufacturers. In contrast, transactions involving beauty services, apparel, and accessories saw substantially larger increases when Christmas shopping was down to the wire.

These category-specific patterns take on added importance in a year when many consumers are managing tighter budgets. The 2026 Consumer Holiday Spending Study from The Strawhecker Group and the Electronic Transactions Association found that 44% of consumers report greater financial stress than last year and 72% plan to set a holiday budget. With shoppers more deliberate about when and how much they spend, knowing which categories peak early versus late can help retailers make sharper decisions on inventory, staffing, and promotions.

“This is a great example of how the combination of Celero and Deluxe can transform data into useful insights for our customers and partners,” said Kevin Jones, president of Deluxe Merchant Services. “Understanding how and when consumers spend empowers businesses to make better decisions about staffing, inventory, and marketing, and we’re in a great position to help small- and medium-sized businesses interpret the data Deluxe has accumulated.”

Across all retail categories analyzed, the increase in transactions between Thanksgiving week and the mid-December shopping period narrowed substantially over the four-year study. In 2022, average transactions per merchant were 17% higher during the peak Christmas shopping week than during Thanksgiving week. That difference narrowed to 16% in 2023 and just 1% in 2024, before recovering modestly to 4% in 2025.

In 2025:

  • Beauty services: Average transactions per merchant increased 18% in the week before Christmas compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Apparel and accessories: Average transactions per merchant increased 20% during Christmas week compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Sporting goods stores processed approximately 18.9% more payment volume per merchant during Thanksgiving week in 2025 than their average weekly volume during the two weeks leading up to Christmas.

The same TSG/ETA study found that 57% of consumers would shop elsewhere or be less likely to return if their preferred payment method wasn’t available—reinforcing that capturing concentrated late-season demand also requires offering the payment options shoppers expect.

PASCAGOULA, Miss.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB), the parent company of TownBridge Bank, reported net income available to common shareholders through the third quarter of 2026 of $12.84 million, or $9.13 per share, compared with earnings of $2.30 million, or $1.73 per share, in the same period of the prior year. Gross income through the third quarter totaled $73.34 million, an increase of 82.02% from the prior year. Balance sheet footings increased by 36.95% to $1.30 billion during the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Net loans grew to $692.90 million over the trailing 12 months from $466.73 million, an increase of 48.46%. Total deposits increased 58.65% during the same period, from $603.81 million at September 30, 2025, to $957.97 million. Significant growth in the balance sheet and in earnings is primarily the result of the successful acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank, Breaux Bridge, LA (FM Bank), which closed on April 1, 2026.

Selected financial highlights:

  • Net loans increased to $692.90 million at the end of the third quarter, up from $677.13 million at the end of the second quarter.
  • Total interest income during the third quarter increased to $16.99 million from $12.67 million during the same period in 2025, an increase of 34.11%. Net interest income for the quarter totaled $13.24 million, compared with $9.69 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Deposit costs totaled 74 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, essentially unchanged from 73 basis points in the second quarter of 2026.
  • The ratio of loans past due 30-89 days stood at 2.54% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026, an increase from 1.70% at the end of the second quarter. The ratio of non-accrual loans totaled 1.87% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.94% at the end of the second quarter. The Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) totaled $7.95 million, or 1.13% of total loans.
  • Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) mark-to-market losses in the securities portfolio totaled ($11.80 million) at the end of the third quarter of 2026, representing 3.05% of the $386.69 million securities portfolio. The increase in AOCI from ($5.81 million) during the second quarter is a result of increases in market rates during the quarter.
  • On-balance sheet liquidity levels remain healthy, with cash and cash equivalents totaling $94.42 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026. In addition to these large cash balances, the Company's investment portfolio remains highly liquid, with a significant portion of the portfolio able to be liquidated with minimal losses.
  • In addition to the sizable on-balance sheet liquidity position, the Company has more than $200 million in additional borrowing capacity at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas and the Federal Reserve.

“We continued a strong earnings trend in the third quarter of 2026, with pre-tax, pre-provision earnings of approximately $2.26 million. This was inclusive of a $158 thousand loss on securities sales as we repositioned the portfolio to better fit the bank after our acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank earlier this year,” remarked Casey Hill, the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He continued: “Core earnings continue to accelerate as we realize certain efficiencies after our most recent merger. We do expect these efficiencies to further materialize as we undergo our core and systems conversion in January of 2027. Since the acquisition of FM Bank, we have been operating two core systems along with several other duplicative systems that, once fully merged, are expected to produce significant cost savings.”

“In addition,” continued Hill, “our teams across our Family of Brands continue to perform well. The increase in revenue from our legacy brands, paired with the continued high performance of the FM Bank team bodes well for continued lift in future earnings. While we are experiencing tailwinds in the form of slight elevations in past due loans, we feel confident that the bulk of these should be resolved prior to year-end and are not indicative of broader erosion in our loan portfolio. We are very optimistic about financial performance going forward.”

“Our third quarter results reflect the strong progress our teams are making in bringing FM Bank into our Family of Brands operating model,” remarked Clayton Legear, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. “Our talented bankers have done an outstanding job of integrating a sizable new brand while continuing to operate our legacy brands at ever stronger levels. We remain encouraged that our operating model allows our brand bankers to serve their clients and communities with the same care and attention they always have and to drive strong results. We are on track for our core systems conversion in January 2027, and we are excited about the enhanced efficiencies and capabilities that will follow.”

Legear continued: “The third quarter also marked an important milestone for our Company. Effective September 28, 2026, our bank charter name officially changed from Merchants & Marine Bank to TownBridge Bank, providing a shared corporate identity for our growing Family of Brands. While our bank charter name has changed, our commitment to our Family of Brands operating model has not. Each of our brands will continue to retain their unique identity, and to be led by local bankers who know their clients, understand their communities, and make decisions close to home. Backed by our Battle-Ready Balance Sheet, our talented team of bankers in every Brand, and the strong momentum building across our Family of Brands, we are better positioned than ever for the future.”

Share Repurchase Program

The share repurchase program authorized by the Board of Directors in the second quarter, covering up to three percent (3%) of the Company's outstanding common stock, remains in effect through June 30, 2027.

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB) is the parent company of TownBridge Bank, a Mississippi chartered community bank serving the Gulf South region. Originally founded in 1899 as Merchants & Marine Bank and reborn during 1932, the Bank adopted the TownBridge Bank name in 2026 to provide a shared charter identity for its growing Family of Brands while allowing its community banking and financial services brands to retain the local identifies, leadership, and relationships that make them distinctive. The Bank offers banking services to customers in Southern Mississippi and Coastal Alabama under its legacy Merchants & Marine Bank brand, in Southeastern Louisiana through its Mississippi River Bank brand, and in the Acadiana Region of Louisiana through its Farmers-Merchants Bank brand. It offers mortgage financing through its Canvas Mortgage brand, cannabis banking through its CannaFirst Financial brand, and access to government-guaranteed credit through its Voyager Lending brand. It provides bank operational, risk, and support services through its Community of Resources bank services brand. For more information on Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc., visit https://townbridge.bank/investors/

The Immersive Holiday Partnership Features Bespoke Frozen Yogurt by Award-winning Chef & Author Andy Baraghani, Personalized Product Experiences & Festive Programming at Bloomingdale’s 59th Street Flagship

ANDY BARAGHANI IMAGES
UGG PARLOR IMAGES
Photography credit: Julia Khoroshilov

SANTA BARBARA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--This holiday season, Southern California-based global lifestyle brand UGG® (a division of Deckers Brands [NYSE: DECK]) is partnering with Bloomingdale’s, Forty Carrots and New York Times bestselling and James Beard Award-winning chef and author, media personality and cultural tastemaker Andy Baraghani to introduce the UGG® Parlor, an unexpected fusion of fashion, food and culture at Forty Carrots. Running November 20 through January 3, the partnership brings a playful new perspective to seasonal traditions, combining Bloomingdale’s retail heritage, Forty Carrots’ cult-favorite frozen yogurt, Baraghani’s distinctive culinary perspective and the UGG® brand’s approach to self-expression.

Andy Baraghani x UGG® Parlor

“At UGG, we believe the most memorable gifts are the ones that create a feeling and bring people together in unexpected ways,” said Tracy Paoletti, Vice President & General Manager, UGG North America. “The UGG Parlor at Forty Carrots brings that philosophy to life by blending fashion, food and self-expression into a festive experience that invites consumers to make the season their own. We’re excited to partner with Bloomingdale’s, Forty Carrots and Andy Baraghani to create a new holiday tradition that celebrates the joy of giving, receiving and sharing something special.”

“I’m very much in favor of a frozen yogurt break in the middle of holiday shopping,” said Andy Baraghani. “Working with UGG and Forty Carrots was a chance to take the nostalgic flavors I love this time of year and give them a little twist. I wanted something seasonal that you’d crave well beyond the holidays. Come to the UGG Parlor, have a frozen yogurt, and stay for a second helping.”

UGG® PARLOR AT FORTY CARROTS AT BLOOMINGDALE’S

At the heart of the creative exchange is a custom frozen yogurt experience featuring two bespoke flavors created in partnership with UGG® and Andy Baraghani. UGGingerbread Spice, the signature UGG® flavor, will be available at all Forty Carrots locations across the U.S. and is the perfect balance of Bloomingdale’s signature frozen yogurt with the warm, nostalgic flavors of gingerbread, featuring notes of ginger, cinnamon, and holiday spice. UGGingerbread Nightcap by Andy Baraghani, an exclusive, bespoke creation imagined by the chef himself, will be available only at Forty Carrots at Bloomingdale’s 59th Street flagship in New York City. Featuring creamy frozen yogurt, gingerbread spice, and a hint of dark rum, it's a holiday nightcap you eat with a spoon. Both flavors will be available through January 3.

The partnership transforms an everyday treat into a festive destination, inviting shoppers to experience the partnership through seasonal flavors, personalized product and thoughtful details throughout the holiday season.

The UGG® Parlor will also come to life through a series of consumer activations, including UGG® customization experiences, frozen yogurt sampling and festive touches designed to encourage discovery and invite guests to make the experience their own.

HOLIDAY EXPERIENCES AT THE UGG® PARLOR

Across five weekends in November and December, UGG® and Forty Carrots will bring the UGG® Parlor to life through a rotating lineup of customization experiences, frozen yogurt sampling and festive treats at Bloomingdale’s 59th Street flagship.

Weekend 1: Holiday Takeover Kickoff — Froyo & Customization

Friday, November 20, 3-8 PM
Saturday, November 21-Sunday, November 22, 12-6 PM

Guests can personalize select Classic boots at the UGG® Customization Studio with laser-engraved designs from a curated holiday flash sheet featuring New York City-inspired and seasonal motifs. A custom-branded frozen yogurt sampling cart will also offer guests a taste of the partnership on the fifth floor of Bloomingdale’s 59th Street location.

Weekend 2: Personalize Your Pair

Saturday, November 28-Sunday, November 29, 12-6 PM

The UGG® Customization Studio will continue offering laser engraving on select Classic boots, inviting guests to personalize their pair with NYC-inspired and holiday designs.

Weekend 3: A Sweet Treat & Personalization

Saturday, December 5, 12-6 PM

On Saturday, December 5, customers who purchase men’s or women’s UGG® footwear in-store will be eligible to receive one complimentary small UGGingerbread Spice frozen yogurt at Forty Carrots. To redeem, customers must present their December 5 in-store purchase receipt at Forty Carrots. Offer is valid for purchases made on December 5 only and applies exclusively to the small UGGingerbread Spice frozen yogurt.

The UGG® Customization Studio will also be available for guests to personalize select Classic boots.

Weekend 4: Festive Personalization

Saturday, December 12-Sunday, December 13, 12-6 PM

Guests can continue to personalize select Classic boots with laser-engraved designs inspired by New York City and the holiday season.

Weekend 5: Holiday Sweets & Personalized Treats

Saturday, December 19-Sunday, December 20, 12-6 PM

The holiday programming will conclude with festive touches throughout Bloomingdale’s, including custom UGG® boot-shaped gingerbread cookies distributed on the Women’s sales floor, custom UGG® holiday cards with purchase and live portrait illustrations of guests wearing UGG® products.

Through January 3, The UGG® Parlor at Forty Carrots celebrates the spirit of holiday gifting through an unexpected blend of fashion, food and self-expression. By bringing together the UGG® brand’s distinctive approach to style, Forty Carrots’ iconic frozen yogurt and Andy Baraghani’s creative culinary perspective, the partnership invites shoppers to discover new seasonal traditions and Gift the Feeling through memorable moments of connection, indulgence and joy.

About UGG®

Founded in 1978 by an Australian surfer on the coast of California, UGG® is a global lifestyle brand renowned for its iconic Classic boot. First worn by Hollywood royalty, fashion editors, and then the world, UGG® designs and retails footwear, apparel, and accessories with an uncompromising attitude toward quality and craftsmanship. Delivering more than $2 billion in annual sales, UGG® partners with the best retailers globally and owns concept and outlet stores worldwide in key markets, including New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Paris, London, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Beijing. For more information, please visit ugg.com @ugg.

About Deckers Brands

Deckers Brands is a global leader in designing, marketing and distributing innovative footwear, apparel and accessories developed for both everyday casual lifestyle use and high-performance activities. The Company's portfolio of brands includes UGG®, HOKA®, and Teva®. Deckers Brands products are sold in more than 50 countries and territories through select department and specialty stores, Company-owned and operated retail stores, and select online stores, including Company-owned websites. Deckers Brands has over 50 years of history building niche footwear brands into lifestyle market leaders, attracting millions of loyal consumers globally. For more information, please visit www.deckers.com.

About Bloomingdale’s

Bloomingdale’s is America’s only nationwide, full-line, upscale department store. A division of Macy’s, Inc. (NYSE: M), it currently operates 31 Bloomingdale’s stores, 25 Bloomingdale’s The Outlet stores, and 4 Bloomie’s stores in California, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia, and Washington. In addition, Bloomingdale’s has an international presence with locations in Dubai and Kuwait. Founded in 1872, the iconic retailer celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2022. Be sure to follow @bloomingdales on social media, become a Loyallist, and for more information, or to shop any time, visit www.bloomingdales.com.

A beloved Bloomingdale’s destination since its debut in 1974, Forty Carrots is best known for its iconic frozen yogurt, alongside a menu of smoothies, salads, sandwiches and more. It has become a signature part of the shopping experience and a longtime favorite among customers.

About Andy Baraghani

Andy Baraghani is a New York Times bestselling and James Beard Award-winning chef, author, media personality and cultural tastemaker. Born in the Bay Area and now deeply enmeshed in the fabric of New York, Andy has become one of the most sought after names in the food world. At the age of 16, he began working at the world renowned restaurant, Chez Panisse. Andy continued his culinary training at the prestigious L’Arpege in Paris and Estela in New York. He is opening his first restaurant called Ditto, in New York City in fall 2026.

Tips to Protect Pipes Before Freezing Temperatures

ALEXANDRIA, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As winter approaches, Virginia American Water reminds customers to prepare their home and pipes, providing handy tips to help avoid costly repairs and unwanted stress from frozen pipes. 

"Customers should prepare for frigid temperatures by taking simple steps to protect their pipes from freezing," said Charlie Piekanski, Vice President of Operations, Virginia American Water. "By taking proactive measures, you can help ensure you and your loved ones stay safe and comfortable when the temperature drops."  

You can prepare now by taking the following steps:  

  • Know how to shut off your water: Locate your main water shut-off valve. In many homes, it is located near the water meter or close to where the water pipe enters the home. Hang an I.D. tag on the valve so it can be found quickly during an emergency. Download a tag to print here.
  • Test your main water shut-off valve: Once located, test the shut-off valve by closing it. Once completely closed, check sinks and other water fixtures to ensure the shut-off valve is working properly.  
    • Ball valves generally only require a quarter turn to close. 
    • Gate valves are generally closed by turning the handle clockwise and should turn easily.  
    • If the valve does not close easily, it may need to be serviced.  
    • Bonus: While you are there, check your incoming water service line material! Virginia American Water is working with customers to identify their service line material. If it is found to be made of lead or galvanized steel, they will be replaced in the future. Visit our website for information.  
  • Check sprinkler or irrigation systems: Make sure everything is turned off and fully drained. 
  • Eliminate sources of cold air near water lines: Check for pipes in areas that might be prone to freezing, such as crawl spaces, unheated rooms, basements, garages, and exterior walls. Fix drafty windows, insulate walls around pipes and plug drafts around doors. 
  • Protect your pipes: Where pipes are exposed to cold, wrap them with insulation or heat tape (even fabric or newspaper can help). 

When temperatures stay below freezing: 

  • Give pipes a helping hand: If pipes run through cabinets or vanities, open the doors to let warmer room temperatures flow in.

You can prepare now by taking the following steps:  

  • Know how to shut off your water: Locate your main water shut-off valve. In many homes, it is located near the water meter or close to where the water pipe enters the home. Hang an I.D. tag on the valve so it can be found quickly during an emergency. Download a tag to print here.
  • Test your main water shut-off valve: Once located, test the shut-off valve by closing it. Once completely closed, check sinks and other water fixtures to ensure the shut-off valve is working properly.  
    • Ball valves generally only require a quarter turn to close. 
    • Gate valves are generally closed by turning the handle clockwise and should turn easily.  
    • If the valve does not close easily, it may need to be serviced.  
    • Bonus: While you are there, check your incoming water service line material! Maryland American Water is working with customers to identify their service line material. If it is found to be made of lead or galvanized steel, they will be replaced in the future. Visit our website for information.  
  • Check sprinkler or irrigation systems: Make sure everything is turned off and fully drained. 
  • Eliminate sources of cold air near water lines: Check for pipes in areas that might be prone to freezing, such as crawl spaces, unheated rooms, basements, garages, and exterior walls. Fix drafty windows, insulate walls around pipes and plug drafts around doors.

WASHINGTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Mark Widmar, chief executive officer of First Solar, Inc. (Nasdaq: FSLR) (“First Solar” or “the Company”), today urged bipartisan support for an industrial strategy and the enforcement of American trade and tax laws to sustain domestic manufacturing growth.

At the invitation of Chairman John Moolenaar (R-Mich.), Widmar testified before the United States House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (the House Select Committee on China).

Addressing the committee at the hearing on “Outproducing the CCP: Restoring American Manufacturing,” Widmar said, “American technology, American factories, American workers, and consistent enforcement of our trade and tax laws are not Democratic priorities or Republican ones. They are American ones.”

First Solar is the country’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company and the only one of the world’s largest solar manufacturers to be headquartered in the US. The Company operates six manufacturing facilities in Alabama, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina; R&D centers in Ohio and California; and a solar technology testing center in Arizona. By the end of 2026, First Solar expects to have invested over $5 billion in American manufacturing and R&D infrastructure since 2019, and by 2027 it forecasts approximately 17 GW of US nameplate module manufacturing capacity.

“First Solar is here as proof that America can rebuild manufacturing capacity,” Widmar said. “We didn’t invest approximately $5 billion in American manufacturing because it was easy. We invested because we believe in the American worker.”

Citing tax and trade policies across multiple administrations that catalyzed domestic solar manufacturing growth, Widmar noted, “The lesson is that industrial strategy must be bipartisan. When the rules hold from one Administration and Congress to the next, entire markets can grow, and domestic manufacturers can invest with certainty in the United States.”

Widmar noted the range of trade remedies available to help level the playing field for American workers and manufacturers and cited the Section 232 action on polysilicon as an example of a targeted remedy — one aimed at a specific national security risk or economic abuse and applied where there is domestic capacity to build. He said, “On behalf of all of our American workers, I thank President Trump and Secretary Lutnick for the first true acknowledgment that the solar supply chain is a national security issue.”

The Top Tier of China’s SME Cultivation System

The MIIT’s gradient cultivation system for high-quality small and medium-sized enterprises (“SMEs”) has three tiers: technology-based and innovative SMEs; specialized and sophisticated SMEs, recognized at the provincial level; and Little Giant enterprises, designated at the national level by the MIIT. The designation is valid for three years, from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029.

MCLEAN, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Appian (Nasdaq: APPN), an AI automation leader, today released new research asking AI decision-makers and IT leaders about AI-assisted development. They found that enterprise investments in fast-tracked AI software development are creating an unexpected drain on corporate innovation capital, with 82% of enterprise leaders allocating at least 10% of their current technology innovation funds to test, deploy, maintain, update, integrate, and/or repair isolated AI software builds.

Enterprise investments in AI software development are creating an unexpected drain on corporate innovation capital.

In the global survey of 851 respondents at large enterprises, Appian defines a new term: "aloneware." These are applications built or modified with AI-assisted development tools outside an approved enterprise platform environment. While these tools accelerate initial code creation, organizations face mounting friction to understand AI-generated applications and keep them functional, secure, and integrated over time.

Upfront speed creates downstream work

Initial build speed is failing to deliver long-term efficiency. Just over seven in 10 (71%1) enterprise leaders surveyed report that while standalone AI tools accelerate development, they are spending more time across testing, system integration, troubleshooting, scaling, and/or deployment.

According to Matt Calkins, CEO of Appian, "Some people get so excited about 'free' software that they forget the risks. Enterprises can now create tech debt faster than ever before."

Aloneware diverts strategic innovation budgets

The operational burden of maintaining software built outside a platform is directly diverting capital away from strategic growth. More than eight in 10 (82%) enterprise leaders surveyed report allocating at least 10% of their current technology innovation budgets to testing, deploying, maintaining, updating, integrating, and/or repairing software built outside a platform environment. And 43% of those surveyed currently allocate at least 20% of the budget—a figure that 64% expect to allocate within the next two years, indicating that the financial drain is accelerating quickly.

Compounding these budget demands, more than two-thirds (68%2) of enterprise leaders report unexpected post-launch costs or resources tied directly to security, governance, and compliance remediation.

The support void and the need for platforms

When isolated AI applications break, organizations face a critical support void. More than two-thirds (68%3) of leaders find it challenging to access accountable technical support when problems arise with applications built outside a platform, while 66%3 report difficulties keeping code, architecture, dependencies, and system integrations up to date.

Against this backdrop, 73%4 of respondents state that a shared architectural foundation would improve their ability to control total cost of ownership and 71%4 say it would help them maintain software over time.

"The most important applications in enterprises need support," Calkins adds. "If you vibe-code them, there will be nobody to turn to when problems occur. Using AI to build applications on a commercial platform combines the speed of AI with the reliability of supported technology."

MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ameriprise Financial, Inc. (NYSE: AMP) has been named one of the “World's Best Employers of 2026” by Forbes. The annual ranking recognizes organizations that excel in employee engagement, talent development, workplace culture and reputation.

"At Ameriprise, our people around the globe are united by a shared commitment to helping clients feel confident about their financial futures," said Kelli Hunter Petruzillo, Executive Vice President of Human Resources at Ameriprise Financial. "We're honored to be recognized among the World's Best Employers. This accolade reflects the strength of our culture, the passion and dedication of our employees, and our continued focus on innovation in service to clients. By investing in our people and creating opportunities for growth and engagement, we're building an environment where employees contribute meaningful work and make a lasting impact.”

Developed by Forbes and Statista, the ranking evaluates multinational organizations with at least 1,000 employees. More than 300,000 employees were surveyed anonymously over the past three years and asked about their willingness to recommend their employer, other employers in their industry and organizations within their social circles.

The recognition adds to a growing list of honors Ameriprise has received from leading third-party organizations for its culture, innovation and business performance, including:

  • TIME “America’s Best Companies” for 2026
  • Newsweek “America’s Greatest Workplaces” for 2026
  • Forbes “America’s Best Companies” for 2026

For more information about careers at Ameriprise, visit ameriprise.com/careers.

About Ameriprise Financial

At Ameriprise Financial, we have been helping people feel confident about their financial future for more than 130 years1. With extensive investment advice, global asset management capabilities and insurance solutions, and a nationwide network of more than 10,000 financial advisors, we have the strength and expertise to serve the full range of individual and institutional investors' financial needs.

1Company founded June 29, 1894.

The 2026 World's Best Employers list was developed by Statista and published in partnership with Forbes. The ranking is based on a proprietary methodology that evaluated multinational employers with at least 1,000 employees operating globally. The analysis incorporated independent survey responses from more than 300,000 employees and other respondents across more than 50 countries, collected from March through May in each of the last three years (2024-2026). Eligible companies were assessed based on direct evaluations from employees and indirect evaluations from respondents familiar with employers in their industry or through friends, family members, and acquaintances. Responses from all three years were included in the analysis, with greater weighting assigned to more recent responses. Ameriprise did not pay a fee to be evaluated, but did pay a fee to publicly cite the results. Find more information at https://www.forbes.com/lists/worlds-best-employers/.

TIME magazine partnered with Statista to recognize America’s Best Companies, chosen based on an independent survey of roughly 217,000 U.S. employees. Eligible companies (those headquartered in the U.S. that generated over $100 million in revenue in 2024 or 2025) were evaluated across three key categories: employee satisfaction, revenue growth and sustainability transparency. The final ranking reflects the period from January 2026 to May 2026. Ameriprise did not pay a fee to be evaluated but did pay a fee to publicly cite the results.

Newsweek partnered with Plant-A Insights Group to recognize America’s Greatest Workplaces, chosen based on an independent survey of roughly 179,000 employees. Eligible companies (U.S. companies employing over 1,000 individuals) were evaluated from April to October 2025, across several categories, including corporate culture; work-life-balance; company image; working environment; belonging and community; sustainability & awareness; compensation & benefits; training & career progression; mental wellbeing; job security. Additionally, results from three previous studies that took place between 2022 and 2024 were integrated into the overall findings with reduced weight. Ameriprise did not pay a fee to be evaluated but did pay a fee to publicly cite the results. For more information: https://rankings.newsweek.com/.

Forbes recognized America's Best Companies based on an evaluation of U.S. headquartered companies across 11 categories: employee and customer sentiment, financial performance, business trajectory, cybersecurity, media sentiment, workforce diversity, sustainability, workforce stability and company size. The top 500 companies were included in the final list. Ameriprise did not pay a fee to be evaluated, but did pay a fee to publicly cite the results. Find more information at https://www.forbes.com/lists/best-companies/.
